title: Boxer Dog Tags for Wiggle Butts & Zoomies | Salty Dog Tags
description: Funny engraved boxer dog tags, laser cut in Lehi, Utah. Built for wiggle butts, drool and zoomies. Name and number on the back. From $12.
blurb: Engraved tags for the dog that greets you with its whole body and never quite finishes being a puppy. Boxers are short-snouted like our bulldogs, just with more springs.

hero.alt: Close-up of a laser-engraved dog tag: polished stainless bone with a paw cut-out, engraved WHISKY and a phone number
hero.figcaption: Whisky's actual tag. He's a bulldog, but the laser doesn't care what breed you are.

tough.h2: Built for zoomies, drool and full-body wiggles
tough.html:
A boxer's tag lives a rough life: slammed into door frames during greetings, dunked in the water bowl, and swung around like a wrecking ball on every zoomie lap.

Our text is laser-cut into the metal, not printed on top. Drool, sweat and a thousand collisions don't peel it off.

The wiggle never stops. Neither does the engraving.

How engraving holds up →

more.h2: Made by a house with seven bulldogs
more.lead: We're a family in Lehi, Utah with seven English bulldogs and one very busy laser. We wrote the bulldog tags first, from experience. Boxers are the closest thing our bulldogs have to athletic cousins. The jokes come from boxer friends who have been knocked over at every greeting.

sayings.note: Every line above fits the tag as written. Want your own? Type it in the builder and the preview shows what fits before you pay.

What to Put on a Dog Tag

items.q: Will drool and water wear off the engraving?
items.a: No. The text is laser engraved into the metal, so there's no ink for drool or water to lift.

items.q: Can I put my boxer's name and my phone number on the tag?
items.a: Yes. Funny saying on the front, name and phone number on the back.

items.q: Do you have sayings written specifically for boxers?
items.a: Eight on this page, about the wiggle, the jumping and the never-ending puppy phase. Each fits the tag as written.

items.q: Boxers overheat. Should the tag say so?
items.a: If your boxer struggles in heat, a back-line note like "Keep me cool" can help a finder. Ask your vet about your own dog's limits.
